_comment: Declared slots that are deliberately NOT covered by a per-slot empty-slot corpus item, each with the reason no conveyor arm can exercise them. The corpus self-check (corpus/run.sh check 2, SLOT ENUM) enumerates declared slots mechanically from the <!-- wf:slot --> markers in every plugin's skill bodies and requires an arm per slot; that requirement assumes the declaring skill is on the SDD conveyor the runner drives (/wf:spec -> /wf:plan -> /wf:tasks -> /wf:implement, plus /wf:ship). A slot declared on a skill outside that conveyor has no arm that could observe it, and a fabricated arm would violate the corpus's founding rule that assertions are born from observations, never speculation. Such a slot is listed here, with a reason, rather than silently unchecked or covered by invented run bytes. This list is NOT a place to park a conveyor slot whose arm is merely unwritten: check 2 fails an exemption whose slot DOES have a corpus item (a stale exemption), and check 9 (BARE CORE) still requires every declared slot to appear in the bare-core arm's own slots_covered/slots_exempt, so an exemption here never removes a slot from that accounting.

exempt.reason: declared in /wf-author-caps:new-skill, an interactive pack-owned scaffolder that is not on the SDD conveyor the runner drives and takes no task id — the runner has no way to invoke it, so no arm can observe its unfilled behavior. Its inertness is asserted instead at the resolver, the layer that actually composes the slot: when wf-core-authoring is unregistered and no override is present, resolve_content({class: "slot", skill: "new-skill", point: "constraints"}) returns {status: "unfilled"}; when wf-core-authoring is registered, its append contribution fills new-skill.constraints. These registration-dependent readings are what the empty-slot arms exist to corroborate. First pack-owned slot in the marketplace (WF-363, C023); registered fill added by WF-368; revisit when the runner can drive a pack scaffolder.

declared in /wf:fleet Closeout, a multi-item orchestrator that is not on the SDD conveyor the runner drives (/wf:spec -> /wf:plan -> /wf:tasks -> /wf:implement, plus /wf:ship). The conveyor arms observe one skill against one seeded task id; a fleet run needs a populated scoreboard, several rows already merged through their own pull requests, and a tracker umbrella, and no fleet invocation has ever been driven through runner/run-skill.sh. An arm authored here would therefore not be a canned copy of an observed run - the disclosure every other arm carries - but bytes invented for a run that has never executed, asserting an invariant nobody measured. That is the false-clean the sweep this slot fills exists to end, so it is not committed in the layer that checks for it. The slot's inertness is asserted instead at the two layers that can observe it without a container: the resolver, where resolve_content({class: "slot", skill: "fleet", point: "closeout-review"}) returns {status: "unfilled"} with pr-review unregistered; and the capability's own fixture suite, whose provider-less case pins the unfilled render (`Review sweep: not attempted`) and the run-block slot guard pins its shape. Revisit when the runner can drive a fleet run against a seeded multi-row scoreboard - the fleet-two-task fixture already seeds that shape for cost measurement and is the natural starting point.
